summary: Removes the read-only attribute from the named file, loads its contents into a stack temp struct via one of two loader variants selected by a3, then dispatches the loaded state to up to four fixed sub-object pointers (this+0x10..0x1C) and to each element of a variable-length sub-object array (this+0x20, stride 200 bytes, count this+0x38) through each object's vtable+8 callback. Returns 0 if at least one sub-object received the data, 1 otherwise. The temp struct is closed and freed on all paths.

local_names.lpFileName: file path whose read-only attribute is cleared before loading
local_names.a3: loader variant selector (nonzero selects sub_566940, zero selects sub_566A70)
local_names.v12: stack temp struct holding loaded file state
local_names.v3: flag: set when at least one sub-object received the data

operations.description: If lpFileName is null, skip loading and dispatch entirely and fall through to return 1.
Clear the FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY attribute (128) on lpFileName via the Win32 attribute-toggle helper before reading the file.
Zero-initialize the stack temp struct (v12) that will hold the loaded file state.
Branch on a3 to select which file-loading variant is used: nonzero picks sub_566940, zero picks sub_566A70.
Load lpFileName into the temp struct using the a3-nonzero loader variant (sub_566940) with arguments (v12, lpFileName, 0, 1, 1).
Load lpFileName into the temp struct using the a3-zero loader variant (sub_566A70) with arguments (v12, lpFileName, 0, 1, 1).
If the temp struct's first field (v12[0]) is nonzero, the file loaded successfully and dispatch to sub-objects may proceed.
Dispatch the loaded state to fixed sub-object 0 held at this+0x10, invoking its vtable+8 callback with (subObject0, v12, 0).
Dispatch the loaded state to fixed sub-object 1 held at this+0x14, invoking its vtable+8 callback with (subObject1, v12, 0).
Dispatch the loaded state to fixed sub-object 2 held at this+0x18, invoking its vtable+8 callback with (subObject2, v12, 0).
Dispatch the loaded state to fixed sub-object 3 held at this+0x1C, invoking its vtable+8 callback with (subObject3, v12, 0).
Set dispatch flag v3 to 1 whenever any sub-object (fixed or array element) received the loaded data.

Iterate the variable-length sub-object array rooted at this+0x20 with element stride 0xC8 (200 bytes) for the count held at this+0x38, dispatching the loaded state to each element's vtable+8 callback with (element, v12, 0).
Close the file handle via the conditional-close dispatcher after data extraction completes.
If v3 indicates at least one sub-object received the data, free the temp struct via SubCallWithConditionalFieldFree and return 0 (success).
Return 0 to signal that the loaded data was dispatched to at least one sub-object.
On the null-filename, failed-load, or no-recipient paths, free the temp struct via SubCallWithConditionalFieldFree before returning 1.
Return 1 to signal that no sub-object received data (null filename, failed load, or no recipient).

unresolved: Semantics of the temp struct's first field (v12[0]) used as the load-success indicator are not specified in evidence.
What each object's vtable+8 callback does with the loaded state is unknown; it is a generic dispatch target.
The meaning of the two loader variants selected by a3 (sub_566940 vs sub_566A70) is unknown; possibly text vs binary or raw vs parsed loading.
The relationship between the fixed sub-objects (this+0x10..0x1C) and the array elements (this+0x20, count this+0x38) is unknown.
Whether callers interpret the return value as success (0) versus no-op (1) is inferred from control flow, not stated by evidence.
